name: cblack34-skills
description: Personal agent skills maintained by Clayton Black.

plugins.name: build-pack
plugins.description: Author strategic build packs, implement them through approved rolling slices, and refactor each passing draft before handoff.

plugins.name: pr-review
plugins.description: Review pull requests and address their review comments: one complete, verified GitHub review with inline severity-labeled comments, and a validate-then-fix loop for every unresolved thread.

plugins.name: gitignore
plugins.description: Create or update a repository .gitignore from gitignore.io templates: always the Windows, macOS, Linux, VS Code, and JetBrains defaults plus the stack templates you name, merged without losing existing custom rules. Use when asked to add or refresh a .gitignore for a language, framework, OS, or editor. Not for ignoring a single path; append that line directly.

plugins.name: laws-of-ux
plugins.description: Design and review user interfaces against the Laws of UX and Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics. Design mode applies them while building or changing a screen, form, flow, or component; review mode hands the UI to a fresh reviewer that reports ranked, evidence-backed findings with fixes. Use whenever building or changing UI, even if UX is not mentioned, and when asked for a UX review, UI review, usability audit, or heuristic evaluation, or when Fitts's Law, Hick's Law, or another Law of UX comes up. Not for visual branding or aesthetics, or a WCAG conformance audit.

plugins.name: tech-writing
plugins.description: Write and rewrite technical documentation that is typed, clear, and concise. Classifies each doc as a Diátaxis tutorial, how-to guide, reference, or explanation, drafts from a short recipe for that type with Google developer style and STE-inspired sentence limits, then runs a ranked review that cuts AI filler, hedging, padding, and stock phrases. Use whenever writing or rewriting a README, guide, tutorial, runbook, API or CLI reference, design doc, ADR, or any other technical doc, even if style is not mentioned. For existing docs, flags what does not conform but rewrites only when asked. Not for marketing copy, fiction, or code comments.
